paper.title: Sample complexity of partition identification using multi-armed bandits

unmapped: Fixed-confidence (delta-PAC) partition identification: decide whether max_i mu_i > u or < u for a known threshold u

settings.name_in_paper: Partition identification (PI) problem with SPEF arms
unmapped: Fixed-confidence (delta-PAC) identification of which component of a known partition of the mean space contains the mean vector
settings.definition_quote: given $ \mu =(\mu_1, \ldots, \mu_K) \in \Omega$, we consider the problem of identifying the correct component  $\mathcal{A}_i$ that contains $\mu$.

algorithms.name: Algorithm 1: D-Tracking sampling with GLR stopping for one-parameter exponential families

bound.regime: mu in A_1 (some mean exceeds u)

symbols.Ku_max: K_1(mu_1|u) = largest KL divergence K_j(mu_j|u) between arm j's distribution and the SPEF member with mean u, among arms (WLOG arm 1)

source.label: the:theorem1
source.quote: Suppose that $(u, \ldots, u) \in {\mathcal U}$. Consider $\mu \in \mathcal{A}_1$ ... Then, \ref{eq:lb-problem} has a unique solution given by $w^*_1 = 1$ ... The lower bound on expected total number of samples generated equals $\frac{1}{K_1(\mu_1 | u)} \times \log (\frac{1}{2.4 \delta}).$

results.notes: Lower bound for delta-PAC algorithms on expected total number of samples. Algorithm class: delta-PAC algorithms.

bound.regime: mu in A_2 (all means below u)

symbols.Ku_i: K_i(mu_i|u): KL divergence between arm i's SPEF distribution and the SPEF member with mean u

source.label: the:theorem1
source.quote: When $\mu \in \mathcal{A}_2$, \ref{eq:lb-problem} has a unique solution given by $w^*_j \propto  1/K_j(\mu_j | u)$, and the lower bound on expected total number of samples generated equals $\sum_{j=1}^K \frac{1}{K_j(\mu_j | u)} \times \log (\frac{1}{2.4 \delta}).$

symbols.T_star: T^*(mu) = 1/C^*(mu), inverse of the optimal value of the max-min lower bound problem LB

conditions: Assumption 1: Lambda_i strictly convex and K_i(mu_i|.) strictly convex in second argument
Assumption 2: K_i(mu_i|nu_i) -> infinity as nu_i -> boundary of U_i
Problem LB has a unique optimal solution (|W(mu)| = 1)
tuning: threshold beta(t,delta) = log(c t/delta) with c large enough

source.label: thm:1-param-exp-fam
source.quote: Suppose that $\Omega \subset \mathcal{U}$ and Assumptions 1 and 2 hold. If \ref{eq:lb-problem} has a unique optimal solution, i.e., if $\abs{\mathcal{W}(\mu)} = 1$, then Algorithm~\ref{alg:1-param-exp-fam} is a $\delta$-PAC algorithm with $$\limsup_{\delta \to 0} \frac{\EE[T_U(\delta)]}{\log\left( \frac{1}{\delta} \right)} \leq  T^*(\mu).$$

results.notes: Asymptotically matches the general lower bound T*(mu) log(1/(2.4 delta)). Also delta-PAC. Compute requires solving Problem LB each step; not stated.

cited_results.cited_title: On the complexity of best-arm identification in multi-armed bandit models
cited_results.setting_description: Fixed-confidence delta-PAC partition identification (transportation inequality): sum_i E[N_i] KL(mu_i||nu_i) >= log(1/(2.4 delta)) for any alternative nu; implies E[total samples] >= T*(mu) log(1/(2.4 delta))
